primitives.name: Monte Carlo Tree Search Configuration Tree
primitives.verbatim_quote: **MCTS search module:** the space is organized as a tree; each node x stores: value v(x) = cumulative score from simulations of the node and all descendants; visit count n_visits(x); stage/depth; solution code σ_sol(x) from the node's simulation.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'x': 'node in configuration tree, dimensionless', 'v(x)': 'cumulative score (normalized metric), [0,1]', 'n_visits(x)': 'number of visits to node x, dimensionless', 'σ_sol(x)': 'solution code at node x, string'}
primitives.assumptions: Pipeline configurations form a hierarchical tree; each node's value reflects cumulative experimental feedback; simulations are independent and identically distributed.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When node visitation becomes sparse or simulation scores diverge significantly from expected values.

layer2.mapping: The MCTS tree is isomorphic to a Bayesian belief network where nodes represent hypotheses and their values reflect posterior probabilities.
layer2.telemetry: Node visit counts and cumulative scores provide empirical validation of belief propagation.

primitives.name: LLM Insight Proposer
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Insight proposer:** LLM reads the problem description + dataset info and generates a search space of candidate insights (preprocessing, feature engineering, model choices).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'I': 'set of candidate insights, dimensionless', 'D': 'dataset metadata, string', 'P': 'problem description, string'}
primitives.assumptions: LLM can abstract valid pipeline components from input data and task descriptions; insights are sufficiently diverse to span configuration space.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When LLM fails to propose meaningful or feasible configurations due to ambiguous inputs or domain mismatch.

layer2.mapping: Generates kernel of possible configurations from semantic embeddings of problem and data, forming basis for MCTS tree expansion.
layer2.telemetry: Insight diversity and coverage of configuration space validated via entropy of generated hypotheses.

primitives.name: MCTS Rollout Cycle
primitives.verbatim_quote: Standard MCTS cycle per rollout: **selection** (descend the tree balancing exploration/exploitation), **expansion** (add child configuration), **simulation** (the LLM executor agent plans, codes, and runs the pipeline for the selected configuration), **backpropagation** (feed the experimental score back up, updating v(x) and n_visits(x) along the path).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'k': 'number of rollouts per night, dimensionless', 'R': 'rollout sequence, set of nodes', 's_i': 'score from simulation i, [0,1]'}
primitives.assumptions: Each rollout is independent; simulation outcomes are deterministic within a fixed codebase; backpropagation correctly updates node statistics.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When rollout paths converge too quickly or fail to explore sufficient diversity in configurations.

layer2.mapping: Rollout cycle mirrors Bayesian updating process, where each simulation acts as a likelihood evaluation and backpropagation updates prior beliefs.
layer2.telemetry: Average score improvement per rollout and convergence rate indicate effective exploration-exploitation trade-off.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core innovation lies in applying Monte Carlo Tree Search (MCTS) to the discrete space of machine learning pipeline configurations. Each node in the tree encodes a specific pipeline setup, with its value representing cumulative performance across simulations. The selection phase uses an upper confidence bound (UCB) strategy to balance exploration of unvisited nodes against exploitation of high-performing ones. Expansion adds new configurations derived from LLM-generated insights, ensuring the search space grows adaptively. Simulation executes these configurations via an LLM executor, returning performance metrics such as normalized score (NS). Backpropagation aggregates these scores upward, refining estimates of node quality. This iterative refinement allows the system to allocate computational resources efficiently across competing hypotheses, avoiding the low-diversity pitfalls of traditional AutoML approaches. The method leverages both structured search and generative modeling to navigate complex, high-dimensional spaces of ML pipelines.
